title: Nicaea, 325: the question
hookLine: bishops, some still scarred from persecution, gather to answer Arius

cards: A priest in Alexandria named Arius is preaching a line that catches on; later writers say his ideas were even set to tunes people could sing. The line, in plain words: there was a time when the Son of God did not exist.
The Father alone has no beginning. The Son came after, the first and greatest of all he made, but made. A creature.
His bishop, Alexander, objects. The quarrel jumps from church to church, city to city, until no single bishop can settle it. Today, the city where the Church gathered to answer: Nicaea.

teach.b: Nicaea was a city in Asia Minor, in what is now Turkey. By the account of the historian Eusebius, the emperor Constantine called bishops there from across his empire.
The Catechism names it the first ecumenical council, and gives its year as 325. Look at who walked in. The historian Theodoret describes some of them.
One bishop, Paul, had lost the use of both hands; a red-hot iron had been put to them under persecution. Others had lost an eye, or been crippled.
Theodoret says the gathering looked like an army of martyrs. Scarred bishops.
Some of these men had paid in their own bodies for saying that Jesus is Lord, and the question in front of them was what, exactly, they meant by it. It's a question from the Gospels.

teach.h: BUT WHOM DO YOU SAY THAT I AM?
teach.b: Jesus asks his disciples, "But whom do you say that I am?" Arius had an answer: someone great, the highest of creatures, but a creature.
The bishops listened, argued, and gave a different answer, the one this path opens tomorrow in a single word. They were not theorists in a comfortable room.

teach.h: ASKED BY PEOPLE WHO HAD SUFFERED.
teach.b: When they asked who he is, they were asking about the one they had suffered for. Catholics believe the Holy Spirit guided that council, and the creed that grew from it is still said at Mass on Sundays.

how: Catholics pray for the pope and their own bishop by name in the Eucharistic Prayer at every Mass, and the Creed said on Sundays grew from the Council of Nicaea.

games.q: you're a bishop who lost an eye for refusing to deny Christ. now the emperor invites you to travel to Nicaea to answer Arius. what do you do?
o: go, scars and all, and help answer the question.
send a letter and let others decide.
games.why: they came. Theodoret says the gathering looked like an army of martyrs.

practice: Bring to mind your own bishop, if you know the name, or the bishops of the world, or the leaders of any community you belong to, sitting today at a table with a question too big for one person.
If you pray, pray for them by name, that they listen well and answer faithfully; if you don't, just hold them in mind with good will for a minute.

wordCard.voice: Nicaea. The city where bishops, some scarred by persecution, met in the first ecumenical council to answer what Arius taught about the Son. Today's word.
